<reflection>
The first experiment at moderate conditions did not strongly discriminate among most mechanisms - most have NLL around -24, indicating the single run is well-fit by nearly all mechanisms. Only M4 and M5 are clearly worse. This is expected since many mechanisms differ only in features (deactivation, product inhibition, catalyst dimerization) that don't manifest strongly at moderate single conditions.

Need experiments that stress specific features:
- Product inhibition → add initial product (distinguishes M12, M17)
- Catalyst order → vary [cat] (distinguishes M2, M3, M13, M19 with cat dimerization)
- Substrate inhibition / high-S effects → high [S] (M7, M11, M16)
- Deactivation vs reversibility → long-time behavior, low catalyst
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
To discriminate among many mechanisms at once, I'll run at high initial product concentration with moderate substrate and catalyst. This tests:
- M12, M17: product binds/deactivates catalyst → slower rate with added P
- M1-type reversible: equilibrium shifts, possibly reverse reaction
- M4: product doesn't matter directly but X-mediated kinetics differ
- Deactivation mechanisms (M9, M13, M14, M18, M20): shouldn't be sensitive to added P
- M11, M16: substrate-induced deactivation, not product

Adding P=0.3 M with S=1.0, cat=0.01 will reveal product-dependent effects broadly.
</hypothesis>
